reason: While this passage from Numbers 13-14 depicts the Hebrew people in great distress and fear regarding the conquest of Canaan, the human leaders do not explicitly tell the people their suffering is their fault. Caleb and Joshua encourage the people and urge them to trust in God, while Moses and Aaron intercede on their behalf (falling on their faces in prayer). Although God ultimately holds the people accountable for their lack of faith and rebellion, pronouncing that those who complained will die in the wilderness, this divine judgment is communicated to Moses rather than directly told to the people as 'your fault.' The blame assignment comes through God's declaration of consequence, not through leaders directly addressing the suffering people and assigning them culpability.
